## Working session summary

I picked up the interrupted work, checked all of issue #7 again point by point, and finished it. PR #8 is now marked ready for review: https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/8. CI passed on the latest commit (checks, workflow lint and tests). Deploy was skipped, which is expected on a pull request. Locally, 104 tests, the lint/format checks and the build all pass, and the PR can merge cleanly with `main`.

**What this session added:**
- **More package registries:** 33 are now checked, up from 20. I added 13 that have no public owner search (Hackage, CPAN, Lean Reservoir, Chocolatey, winget, the Chrome Web Store and others). I scanned all 735 repositories for the files each one needs to publish a package, then looked up the accounts and package names. Each lookup was first tried on a known publisher, so an empty answer means no packages rather than a broken query. None of the 13 has konard packages, and no registry is left unchecked.
- **Blog pictures saved locally:** VK image links stop working within about a day, so a post archived only as links would lose its pictures. The 25 pictures are now saved in the site itself under `/archive/media/`, and the blog shows those copies. Two VK pictures return 404 even on the live posts, so they couldn't be saved. They show a "Picture no longer available" note instead of a broken image.
- **The case study:** `docs/case-studies/issue-7/README.md` now covers the issue quote, every requirement with its solution, evidence and status, the root causes, the limits, the online research and existing components, and screenshots of every page. The blog screenshots were re-taken and two new ones added.
- **PR description:** I rewrote the title and description with a table of all 20 requirements, steps to verify and the screenshots. It keeps "Fixes #7".

**Limits, also listed in the PR and case study:**
- GitHub Packages download counts are approximate because the token lacks the `read:packages` scope.
- The X timeline needs a login, so tweets have to be added by URL in `post-urls.txt`.
- `t.me/drakonard` is a personal account, not a public channel, so there is nothing on Telegram to archive yet.
- VK posts can't be embedded without a per-post code that only logged-in users get, so they are shown from the archive instead.

None of these blocks a requirement, but Telegram content will only appear once a public channel exists.
